Non-surgical · Injectable fillers

Breast Dermal Fillers: Safety, Evidence & Alternatives

Dermal fillers are injectable products used for certain approved aesthetic indications. Their use for breast enlargement is a different matter and is not established, approved or routine.

Home/Non-surgical/Dermal fillers

Regulatory position

The FDA advises against using dermal fillers or other injectable fillers to increase breast size. Serious complications from inappropriate body injections can include infection, persistent pain, tissue damage, scarring, deformity and potentially life-threatening events.

What dermal fillers are

Dermal fillers are injectable products used for certain approved aesthetic indications, depending on the product and the jurisdiction. Different products have different compositions, behaviours and licensed uses.

Why breast use is different

An approval for facial use does not imply suitability for injection into the breasts. The breast is a different anatomical site with different considerations, and the consequences of complications can be more difficult to manage. Because of this, breast filler injections should not be advertised or presented as a routine breast-enlargement service.

Questions

Dermal filler FAQs

Dermal fillers are not approved for breast enlargement. Regulators advise against using them for this purpose because of potentially serious complications.

Alternatives with clearer evidence for increasing breast volume include surgical options such as implants or, in selected cases, autologous fat transfer. Suitability depends on individual factors and should be assessed by an appropriately qualified clinician.
